thread_title: S. leucophylla alba (slightly "hybridy") Baldwin Co, AL
breadcrumb: S. leucophylla alba (slightly "hybridy") Baldwin Co, AL

posts.body_html:
So, is this a pure leucophylla var. alba, or does it have something mixed in it from several generations back? Well, if I had to guess, probability-wise, most Sarracenia in existence likely crossed with another species at one point and then back crossed so many times you can't tell. This individual below is a great example: it totally looks like a pure leucophylla, but it has some alata or rubra wherryi look to it. Hard to say what's going on here.

Interestingly enough, the photos below are summer traps! All of the fall pitchers were burned in the heat wave, so I didn't get the chance to see the real show. Oh well, there's always next year. Photos taken 7/13/15:

posts.body_html: One of my off the wall conjectures is that introgression with rubra and / or alata has been important for the development of alba leucos byreducing the density of veining and thereby making the white more prominent. I'm probably high but I'll throw that one out there!
